label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below typical thresholds, near-minimal depression on the PHQ-9, and virtually negligible anxiety on the GAD-7. Their moderate daily screen time (1–3 hours) suggests balanced digital habits.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78, indicating minimal social isolation)
Exhibits near-floor depressive symptom levels (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.25)
Shows virtually no anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04)
Maintains moderate and controlled screen time of 1–3 hours daily
Highly educated, holding a graduate degree or above
tone: Stable, emotionally resilient, and socially connected

label: Lonely, Distressed High-Screen-Time Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean ≈ 1.69), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean ≈ 1.68), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean ≈ 2.15) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. The profile comprises 178 respondents from the training sample.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness as measured by UCLA-8 (mean ≈ 1.69)
Notably high anxiety symptoms on GAD-7 (mean ≈ 2.15, the highest indicator in the profile)
Extended daily screen time of more than 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded psychological distress
tone: Concerned and empathetic; the data point to a vulnerable group experiencing multiple overlapping mental health challenges alongside heavy screen use

label: Well-Adjusted Female Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging around 1.22, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores around 0.83 (all near the low end of their respective scales), these individuals demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Demonstrates low anxiety levels well below clinical thresholds
Maintains moderate and controlled screen or internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
Psychological well-being scores are consistently low across all distress measures
